newsitem.title: TUNISIA: General Mediterranean hldg opens Occidental hotel.
newsitem.headline: General Mediterranean hldg opens Occidental hotel.

text.p: Luxembourg-base General Mediterranean Holding GMH said it has opened this week a five-star hotel in the Tunisian resort of Hammamet as part of a leisure complex it is establishing there with an investment of at least $45 million.
The 600-bed hotel is managed by the Madrid-based Occidental Hoteles, a GMH subsidiary. It is the 62th Occidental hotel in the world, Occidental-Hammamet manager Jamel Chaieb said.

GMH officials said that the holding has so far invested $45 million in the hotel and a casino which is to be opened there later in November. The cost do not include 100 residential villas being constructed near the hotel and the casino.

They added that the casino is to be run by Cleopatra Palace Ltd, a Dublin-registered company 70 percent-owned by the U.S.' Nona Morelli II with the rest of the capital coming from US and Arab private shareholders.
GMH officials said Cleopatra Palace Ltd plans to market Tunisian holidays in the Gulf, the US and Canada and a European-style entertainment center as part of the leisure complex.
Hammamet, on the southern Mediterranean cost, is at 60 km from Tunis, the capital. It is one of the most popular destinations for holidayers from Europe and the Middle East.
GMH's chairman, Nadhmi Auchi, said at the ceremony inaugurating Occidental-Hammamet on Saturday night that his group plans additional investments in Tunisia, but did not give details.
He said that GMH's portfolio includes finance, banking, property, construction, hotels, tourism, freight, shipping, air transport, commerce, food and pharmaceutical interests.
The group's assets stand at more than $1.2 billion, he said.
